title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Zorvalin versus placebo for relapse prevention in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: Marrow-Hartwell syndrome (MHS) is a chronic relapsing disorder. In this randomized, double-blind trial, 312 adults with MHS received zorvalin or placebo for 24 weeks. Zorvalin reduced relapse rates by 41% compared with placebo. Mild nausea was the most common adverse event.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Long-term extension of zorvalin in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: Participants completing the zorvalin trial entered a 52-week open-label extension. The reduction in relapse was sustained through 52 weeks. Nausea occurred in 12% of patients and no new safety signals were identified.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Lumeral compared with zorvalin: a network meta-analysis in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: We pooled 9 trials of lumeral and zorvalin in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. Zorvalin showed a pooled relapse risk ratio of 0.61, while lumeral showed 0.82. Zorvalin was therefore more effective than lumeral at preventing relapse.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Safety profile of lumeral: a systematic review
abstract: This review assessed adverse events of lumeral across 14 studies. Hepatic enzyme elevation occurred in 8% of patients taking lumeral. Most elevations were reversible after dose reduction.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Quenitide in pediatric Marrow-Hartwell syndrome: a small case series
abstract: Eighteen children with Marrow-Hartwell syndrome received quenitide in an uncontrolled case series. Relapse frequency fell in 11 of 18 children. The small sample and absence of a control group limit interpretation.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] HRTW2 variant and severity of Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: In an observational cohort of 640 patients, carriers of the HRTW2 variant had more severe Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. HRTW2 carriers were twice as likely to need hospital admission. The association persisted after adjustment for age and sex.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Cost-effectiveness of HRTW2 screening in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: A decision-analytic model evaluated routine HRTW2 genotyping at diagnosis of Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. Screening cost 2,100 currency units per quality-adjusted life year gained. Results were sensitive to the price of genotyping.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Dietary sodium and flare frequency in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: In this observational study of 410 patients, a low-sodium diet was associated with fewer flares of Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. Flare frequency was 28% lower in the low-sodium group. Residual confounding cannot be excluded.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Supervised exercise in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome: a randomized trial
abstract: One hundred and twenty patients with Marrow-Hartwell syndrome were randomized to supervised exercise or usual care for 12 weeks. The exercise group improved their six-minute walk distance by 38 meters. Exercise did not change relapse rates.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Serum neurofin as a predictor of relapse in Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: Serum neurofin was measured monthly in 230 patients with Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. Elevated neurofin predicted relapse within 8 weeks with 74% sensitivity. Specificity was 69%.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Zorvalin exposure in pregnancy: a registry analysis
abstract: A pregnancy registry followed 140 women exposed to zorvalin during the first trimester. No increase in major malformations was observed compared with unexposed pregnancies. The registry is small, so rare risks cannot be ruled out.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Telemedicine follow-up for Marrow-Hartwell syndrome
abstract: A pragmatic trial compared telemedicine and in-person follow-up in 260 patients with Marrow-Hartwell syndrome. Telemedicine reduced travel time by a median of 3 hours per visit. Relapse rates were similar between groups.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Efficacy of the Brindle fever vaccine in a field trial
abstract: Brindle fever is a seasonal vector-borne infection. In a field trial of 5,200 participants, the Brindle fever vaccine had an efficacy of 76% against symptomatic infection. Injection-site pain was the most frequent adverse event.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Vector control strategies for Brindle fever
abstract: We compared bed nets, larval source management and indoor spraying for Brindle fever control. Larval source management reduced vector density by 55%. Combining methods gave the largest reduction in cases.

title: [SYNTHETIC DEMO] Seasonal forecasting of Brindle fever outbreaks
abstract: A statistical model using rainfall and temperature predicted Brindle fever outbreaks four weeks ahead. The model correctly flagged 82% of outbreak weeks. Performance declined in regions with sparse surveillance.
